subject: Clarification: deployment demarcation + evidence walkthrough for SOC 2/SIG
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridian-security.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 / SIG ask: network demarcation and isolation models for Dedicated/Private

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call earlier. The Veridian SOC 2 team is compiling the SIG/CAIQ evidence set for our vendor assessment and we need a concise architecture bundle that highlights the following for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private deployments:

- High-level network demarcation (control plane vs. data plane)
- Tenant isolation model (how compute/network boundaries are enforced)
- Typical egress controls and key management boundary points
- Any operational procedures (lift/shift, rollback, tenant eviction) that affect isolation claims

Can you provide an annotated diagram and a short matrix that maps each claim to evidence artifacts (configs, runbooks, logs)? Ideally by end of next week — we have an internal milestone on 2025-06-30.

If there are staged artifacts (draft diagram + formal pack), tell us the expected handoff cadence. We'll upload anything you send to the SIG portal (REQ-3948).

Thanks,

Ellen Park
Security Assurance Lead
Veridian Technologies

Attachment: request_template.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridian-security.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG ask: network demarcation and isolation models for Dedicated/Private

Hi Ellen —

Appreciate the clear checklist. We'll deliver a two-stage package:

1) Draft (by 2025-06-24): annotated topology PDF + a segmentation matrix (spreadsheet) tying claims to artifacts.
2) Formal submission (by 2025-06-30): packaged evidence (configs, runbooks, sanitized logs) and the final CAIQ/SIG crosswalk.

Looping in Kimberly (security architecture) for the topology and Marissa (solutions) for operational runbooks.

Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
- Do you need tenant-level crypto (KMS) diagrams for both hosted Dedicated and on-prem Private, or just the control-plane boundary?
- Are we expected to provide raw network ACLs, or a sanitized snapshot plus an explanation of enforcement?

We'll include the annotated diagram and a minimal ASCII demarcation in the draft so reviewers can quickly understand isolation controls.

Naomi Feldman
Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: controlplane_topology_v1.pdf (attached in draft)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridian-security.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG ask: network demarcation and isolation models for Dedicated/Private

Naomi / Marissa / Ellen —

Attaching the draft artifacts for the request. High-level notes below and a short inline diagram for quick context.

Key assertions (short):
- Control plane (managed by Redwood) is logically separated from customer data plane. Control plane components live in a private management VPC with restricted IGW egress; mutual TLS and per-cluster client certs are used for RPC between control and data plane.
- Data plane for Dedicated: customer workloads run in dedicated tenant pools (GPU nodes) inside a tenant VPC/subnet with enforceable NSGs and host-level isolation via cgroups + container sandboxes.
- Data plane for Private (VPC/on‑prem): customer-managed network, but Redwood agents enforce application-level fences; we document the inbound/outbound contracts and recommend egress filtering patterns.
- KMS boundary: customer-managed KMS keys are supported for Private and Dedicated (bring-your-own-key). We document where key IDs are referenced and how key access is mediated by service identities.

Minimal ASCII demarcation (draft):

[Control Plane - Management VPC] --mutual-TLS--> [Edge Ingress / Router] --VRF/NSG--> [Tenant Pool (Dedicated)]
                                         
[Private Customer VPC / On‑prem] --agent-tunnel--> [Redwood Sidecar / Local Proxy] --app-level ACLs--> [Tenant Runtime]

Files attached in this draft: segmentation_matrix_v2.xlsx (claim -> artifact mapping), deployment_demarcation_diagram.svg (annotated), redwood_controlplane_topology_v1.pdf (topology narrative).

Evidence notes for SIG/CAIQ: for network claims we include:
- sanitized NAT/ACL snapshots (redacted CIDR specifics)
- runbook pointer (runbook/id: RB-472) describing tenant eviction and rollback steps
- short log exemplar (sanitized) showing control-plane RPC auth success for a tenant activation event

Linking the draft folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-veridian-evidence (read-only link will be provisioned to your SOC2 reviewers).

Marissa — please confirm the runbook export (RB-472) and whether we can include a sanitized ACL snapshot in the formal pack.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: segmentation_matrix_v2.xlsx; deployment_demarcation_diagram.svg; redwood_controlplane_topology_v1.pdf
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridian-security.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-23T17:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG ask: network demarcation and isolation models for Dedicated/Private

Kimberly — this looks great and exactly the level of detail we need for the SIG reviewers. A couple of quick clarifications before we kick off the upload:

1) For the sanitized ACL snapshot: we prefer a CIDR-masked CSV + clear mapping to the enforcement point (NSG ID). If RB-472 references specific runbook steps, please include the step ids we should cite in the SIG attachments.
2) For KMS: if the diagram can call out where customer-supplied keys are referenced (no keys themselves) that will satisfy the criteria.

If you can confirm those two items, we'll upload the draft bundle to REQ-3948 and request a preliminary review from our SIG specialist next week.

Thanks — Ellen

Attachment: REQ-3948 (portal ticket)
